title: Free plan vs free trial vs reverse trial
decision_task: Which try-before-you-buy model to use for a self-serve product or a sampleable service, given acquisition, conversion speed and cash needs. / Which free-access configuration a self-serve product should test, and which conversion reference applies to it.
applies_when: Self-serve software, app or digital product
Service businesses considering a free first session or sample (by analogy)
Owner debating freemium vs trial, or conversion from free is low
Self-serve software with clear paid features
Low marginal cost per free user, or a budget for it
A free tier that is useful on its own (needed as the fallback in a reverse trial)
exclusions: High-touch sales where trials are run by hand anyway
Free usage carries material variable cost the business can't fund
Value can't be experienced within any trial length and there's no free tier option
High serving cost per free user with no cost cap (AI inference); her 2026 post argues free still pays at Lovable but its conditions are paywalled
Sales-led, high-price products where self-serve is only defensive
No meaningful free tier to fall back to
High risk of repeat-account abuse without a control
required_inputs: Product analytics for signup, first value and conversion
Billing or plan system that supports time-limited entitlements and a clean downgrade
Profiling to pick team vs individual trial where relevant (EV-C5)
evidence_requirements: Visitor-to-signup and signup-to-paid rates by model (owner data, or labelled fallbacks from base-rates.md)
Whether value grows with more users (virality/network)
Current model and conversion by signup cohort
Whether free users ever see paid features
Post-trial free retention if already running a trial
missing_data_behavior: No visitor counts: compare models qualitatively; no per-visitor estimate.
Two weak references disagree near the observed rate: verdict 'unknown', not 'weak'.
alternatives_when_constrained: Low traffic: sequential before/after with whole-week cohorts and caveats
No gating ability: time-limited trial by account flag
Service business: paid first session at a discount instead of free
Missing data: measure current conversion by cohort first
Low traffic: switch all new signups and compare before/after cohorts, labelled observational
No integration: if plans cannot be time-limited, this is an engineering task, not a ClimbOS action
Small budget: no media spend needed; watch serving cost

decision_branches.if: Value is felt within days and acquisition matters
decision_branches.then: Reverse trial (full access, then a useful free tier).

decision_branches.if: Free users cost real money to serve and there's no cap

decision_branches.then: Freemium or a long trial; judge on paid per 1,000 visitors.

implementation_steps: Measure time to first value; if longer than a plausible trial, lean freemium or reverse trial
Estimate paid customers per 1,000 visitors for each model using owner data or labelled assumptions
Account for timing: trials convert sooner, which matters if cash funds acquisition
Consider a reverse trial: full features for a limited time, then a free tier
Test one model change for new signups only; compare paid per visitor, not paid per signup
If freemium converts poorly and free users rarely see paid features, test a reverse trial for new signups: paid features for a fixed period, no card, then free
State the end date and what happens at the end on the trial screen; list paid benefits over free
Measure paid conversion and post-downgrade free retention for the same cohorts
Cap and watch cost per free user and duplicate accounts
dependencies: A free tier useful on its own (reverse trial)
metrics: Retention of converted users by model
Paid conversion within the cohort window
guardrails: Never compare trial and freemium conversion rates directly (different denominators)
Clear notice before a trial ends; no silent card charge
No silent auto-charge: no-card by default
Clear end date and downgrade terms
observation_window: At least two full trial lengths plus a 30–60 day window for freemium conversions; whole weeks. / Trial length plus one billing period, for both the old and new cohorts to mature.
stop_conditions: Paid per visitor falls versus baseline after the window: revert
Free-user cost exceeds the agreed budget: tighten the free tier
Support load from downgrades spikes: improve messaging
Paid conversion not above the old baseline once cohorts mature
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: Plan engine activation/conversion stage; PB-activation-repair (alternative branch); calculator for paid-per-visitor comparison; base-rates.md fallbacks. / shared/agents/diagnosis.ts REF.trialToPaid and REF.freeToPaid; skills/growth-plays/reference/base-rates.md rows for free plan, no-card trial, card trial; proposed PB-reverse-trial; PB-pricing-test.

interpretation: Interpretation: the useful decision variable is paid customers per visitor over a fixed window, with conversion timing as a cash factor; the reverse trial is a hedge when time-to-value is short but acquisition matters.

INTERPRETATION: Diagnosis compares every SaaS lead-to-paid rate with the no-card trial range. A reverse trial is a different model, and Verna's own figure for trials is lower than ClimbOS's, so the verdict near the boundary is not reliable.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed ClimbOS rule: trial-model recommendations must compute paid per 1,000 visitors and days to cash for each candidate, and must never compare per-trial and per-free-user conversion directly.

PROPOSED RULE: Add freeModel: 'freemium' | 'opt_in_trial' | 'card_trial' | 'reverse_trial' | 'none' to the owner profile and pick the reference by model. Store Verna's 3–5% freemium and 10–15% trial/reverse trial as 'author benchmark, unsourced, Oct 2024, dated'. When two weak references disagree and the rate falls between them, set verdict 'unknown' rather than 'weak'.
disagreements: Base-rates implies a much larger gap (roughly 3–12x) between trial and free-plan conversion than GU-06's 2–3x. Not contradictory: different denominators and sources. Resolve by using owner data and per-visitor comparison.

ClimbOS no-card trial 15–25% vs Verna's 10–15% for trial or reverse trial. Freemium ranges broadly agree (2–5% vs 3–5%). Her freemium/AI-cost conditions are paywalled, so the cost-related avoid_when is ClimbOS's own caution.
